name: PCF8575
full_name: Remote 16-bit I/O expander for I2C and SMBus with interrupt output
description: 16-bit quasi-bidirectional I/O expander on I2C/SMBus, the 16-channel sibling of the PCF8574. Two 8-bit ports (P00-P07, P10-P17), three address pins (A0-A2) for up to eight devices (128 I/O on one bus), and an open-drain INT that flags input changes. 400 kHz Fast-mode I2C, 2.5-5.5 V, low 10 uA standby. Its outputs have high-current drive with a current source to VCC, so it can actively drive LEDs high, not only sink like the PCF8574. Ports are accessed as two bytes (P0 then P1). SMD only - no DIP.

pins.name: INT
pins.description: active-low open-drain interrupt on input change

pins.name: A0
pins.description: address select bit 0 (note: pin 21, not beside A1/A2)

SSOP-24.notes: also DBQ/DGV SSOP/TVSOP, DW SOIC-24, PW TSSOP-24, RGV VQFN-24 (RGN has a different pin numbering).

extra.drive: high-current LED drive + current source to VCC for actively driving high

typical_application: Add 16 GPIO over I2C, directly drive LEDs (source or sink), or expand inputs with change-interrupt; cascade up to eight for 128 I/O on one bus. Read/write both ports as a 2-byte transfer (P0 low byte, P1 high byte).
gotchas: quasi-bidirectional like the PCF8574: to use a pin as an input, first write a 1 to it - there is no direction register
accessed as TWO bytes per transfer (P0 then P1); a 1-byte read/write only touches port 0
NO DIP package - SSOP/TSSOP/SOIC/VQFN only; use a breakout board for through-hole prototyping
answers at 0x20-0x27, the SAME block as the PCF8574 (not the PCF8574A's 0x38-0x3F), so a PCF8574 and PCF8575 can collide on a bus
pinout quirk: A0 is pin 21, far from A1/A2 (pins 2-3) - easy to miswire
no internal I2C pull-ups; INT is open-drain - both need external pull-ups
